_comment: Bundled fallback. The live copy is fetched from addsaltandco.com/cache/rules/v1.json. EVERY rule here is a community-observed pattern, not published issuer policy — see docs/research/domain-rules.md. Nothing has had a domain-expert pass yet; that is a blocking launch item.

rules.explanation: Chase declines almost every application once you've opened 5 or more personal cards at any issuer in the last 24 months. Business cards from most issuers don't count because they don't report to personal bureaus — but Capital One, Discover and TD business cards do.
rules.sourceNote: Thousands of consistent community datapoints over a decade. Authorized-user cards count, though they can sometimes be argued off on reconsideration.

rules.explanation: Chase rarely approves more than two of its own cards in any 30-day period.
rules.sourceNote: Consistent pattern with a meaningful exception rate.

rules.name: 48-month rule
rules.explanation: No new welcome bonus on a Chase product if you received one on that product in the past 48 months. The Sapphire family shares a single bonus across Preferred and Reserve.
rules.sourceNote: Stated in Chase offer terms for the Sapphire family; well-established elsewhere.

rules.name: Once per lifetime
rules.explanation: One welcome bonus per card product, ever. Amex offer terms use "have or have had" language. Personal and business versions of a card are separate products with separate lifetimes.
rules.sourceNote: Stated in Amex offer terms. The single most consequential rule in the hobby — an accidental re-application burns the bonus permanently.

rules.explanation: No more than two Amex credit cards approved in any 90 days.

rules.name: 5 credit card limit
rules.explanation: Amex generally caps you at about five open credit cards at once. Charge cards are counted separately, with a higher limit.
rules.sourceNote: Widely reported; the exact cap varies by relationship.

rules.explanation: No more than one Citi card approved in any 8 days.
rules.sourceNote: Long-standing community consensus. Modelled here as a one-month window, which is more conservative than the true 8 days.

rules.explanation: No more than two Citi cards approved in any 65 days.

rules.name: 48-month family rule
rules.explanation: No bonus if you opened OR CLOSED a card in the same Citi family in the past 48 months. Closing counts, which trips people constantly — tidying up an old card restarts the clock.
rules.sourceNote: Stated in Citi offer terms for several families; well-established across the rest.

rules.explanation: Capital One generally approves about one personal card every six months.
rules.sourceNote: Consistent pattern with a meaningful exception rate. Capital One also pulls all three credit bureaus, costing an inquiry on each.

rules.explanation: No more than two Capital One applications in any 30 days.
Part of Bank of America's 2/3/4 rule: no more than 2 of its cards in 30 days, 3 in 12 months, or 4 in 24 months.
rules.sourceNote: Well-established. Only the 12-month leg is modelled here; the 30-day and 24-month legs are tracked separately.

rules.name: 4/24 (own cards)
rules.explanation: The 24-month leg of Bank of America's 2/3/4 rule: no more than four of its cards in 24 months.
Bank of America declines applicants with 7 or more new accounts at any issuer in the last 12 months. Preferred Rewards members are treated more leniently.
rules.sourceNote: Community-observed, with a meaningful exception rate for existing customers.

rules.explanation: Barclays is sensitive to 6 or more new accounts across all issuers in 24 months. There's no formal published rule — it behaves like a soft threshold rather than a hard cut-off.
rules.sourceNote: Community-observed. Barclays is also notably inquiry-sensitive.

rules.name: Inquiry sensitivity
rules.explanation: U.S. Bank has no formal velocity rule, but declines correlate strongly with recent account and inquiry volume. Applicants with an existing banking relationship fare better.
rules.sourceNote: Datapoints conflict. Treated as a caution, not a cut-off.
